sanskrit: prātar agnim prātar indraṁ havāmahe prātar mitrāvaruṇā prātar aśvinā | prātar bhagam pūṣaṇam brahmaṇas patim prātaḥ somam uta rudraṁ huvema ||
english: At dawn we invoke Agni, at dawn Indra, at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa, at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, the Lord of Prayer, at dawn Soma, and also Rudra we call.

sanskrit: prātarjitam bhagam ugraṁ huvema vayam putram aditer yo vidhartā | ādhraś cid yam manyamānas turaś cid rājā cid yam bhagam bhakṣīty āha ||
english: We invoke Bhaga the mighty, won at dawn, son of Aditi, who apportions — even the impoverished man, even the swift warrior, even the king, says of him: 'May I obtain Bhaga's share.'

sanskrit: bhaga praṇetar bhaga satyarādho bhagemāṁ dhiyam ud avā dadan naḥ | bhaga pra ṇo janaya gobhir aśvair bhaga pra nṛbhir nṛvantaḥ syāma ||
english: O Bhaga, guide and leader, Bhaga of true bounty — lift up and sustain this our prayer; O Bhaga, enrich us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, make us strong with men, that we may be heroes.

sanskrit: utedānīm bhagavantaḥ syāmota prapitva uta madhye ahnām | utodītā maghavan sūryasya vayaṁ devānāṁ sumatau syāma ||
english: May we be possessed of Bhaga now, and at the departure of day, and in its middle; and, O Bountiful One, at the rising of the sun — may we dwell in the favour of the gods.

sanskrit: bhaga eva bhagavām̐ astu devās tena vayam bhagavantaḥ syāma | taṁ tvā bhaga sarva ij johavīti sa no bhaga puraetā bhaviha ||
english: May Bhaga alone among the gods be the possessor of fortune — through him may we be fortunate; 'thee, O Bhaga, all men everywhere invoke' — be thou, O Bhaga, our forerunner here.

sanskrit: sam adhvarāyoṣaso namanta dadhikrāveva śucaye padāya | arvācīnam vasuvidam bhagaṁ no ratham ivāśvā vājina ā vahantu ||
english: The Dawns bow down together for the sacrifice, as Dadhikrāvan hastens to the lustrous track; may prize-winning steeds bring Bhaga, the finder of wealth, toward us — as horses draw a chariot.

sanskrit: aśvāvatīr gomatīr na uṣāso vīravatīḥ sadam ucchantu bhadrāḥ | ghṛtaṁ duhānā viśvataḥ prapītā yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in heroes — auspicious Dawns, may they always shine for us; yielding ghee, well-nourished on every side — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: pra brahmāṇo aṅgiraso nakṣanta pra krandanur nabhanyasya vetu | pra dhenava udapruto navanta yujyātām adrī adhvarasya peśaḥ ||
english: Let the Brahman-priests, the Aṅgirases, go forth; let the roaring of the celestial one advance; let the swelling milk-cows low — may the two press-stones be yoked, the ornament of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sugas te agne sanavitto adhvā yukṣvā sute harito rohitaś ca | ye vā sadmann aruṣā vīravāho huve devānāṁ janīmāni sattaḥ ||
english: Thy path, O Agni, is well-trodden and renowned; yoke thy tawny and thy red horses at the pressing; those ruddy ones who, seated in the dwelling, carry heroes — I invoke the birthplaces of the gods.

sanskrit: sam u vo yajñam mahayan namobhiḥ pra hotā mandro ririca upāke | yajasva su purvaṇīka devān ā yajñiyām aramatim vavṛtyāḥ ||
english: Magnifying your sacrifice with homage, the joyful Hotṛ has raised his voice in the near presence; O thou of many faces, sacrifice well to the gods — may thou attract holy Aramati to the rite.

sanskrit: yadā vīrasya revato duroṇe syonaśīr atithir ācaketat | suprīto agniḥ sudhito dama ā sa viśe dāti vāryam iyatyai ||
english: When, resting softly, the guest Agni comes to presence in the home of the prosperous hero — Agni well-pleased, well-kindled in the house, gives the desirable boon to the people who come before him.

sanskrit: imaṁ no agne adhvaraṁ juṣasva marutsv indre yaśasaṁ kṛdhī naḥ | ā naktā barhiḥ sadatām uṣāsośantā mitrāvaruṇā yajeha ||
english: O Agni, favour this our sacrifice; make us glorious among the Maruts and Indra; let Night and Dawn come to sit upon the sacred grass — here let me worship Mitra and Varuṇa who bring peace.

sanskrit: evāgniṁ sahasyaṁ vasiṣṭho rāyaskāmo viśvapsnyasya staut | iṣaṁ rayim paprathaḍ vājam asme yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Thus Vasiṣṭha, desiring riches, has praised Agni the mighty, giver of all nourishment; may he spread out vigour, wealth, and strength among us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: pra vo yajñeṣu devayanto arcan dyāvā namobhiḥ pṛthivī iṣadhyai | yeṣāṁ brahmāṇy asamāni viprā viṣvag viyanti vanino na śākhāḥ ||
english: Those who love the gods have sung your praise at the sacrifices, with homage to Heaven and Earth for refreshment — those whose prayers spread abroad in every direction like the boughs of a great tree.

sanskrit: pra yajña etu hetvo na saptir ud yacchadvaṁ samanaso ghṛtācīḥ ||stṛṇīta barhir adhvarāya sādhūrdhvā śocīṁṣi devayūny asthuḥ ||
english: Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift racehorse; uplift, O like-minded ones, the ghee-sprinkled ladles; spread the sacred grass well for the rite — the god-seeking flames have risen upward.

sanskrit: ā putrāso na mātaraṁ vibhṛtrāḥ sānau devāso barhiṣaḥ sadantu | ā viśvācī vidathyām anaktv agne mā no devatātā mṛdhas kaḥ ||
english: Let the gods sit upon the ridge of the sacred grass like sons coming to their mother, bearing gifts; let Viśvācī anoint the assembly — O Agni, let there be no failure in our worship of the gods.

sanskrit: te sīṣapanta joṣam ā yajatrā ṛtasya dhārāḥ sudughā duhānāḥ | jyeṣṭhaṁ vo adya maha ā vasūnām ā gantana samanaso yati ṣṭha ||
english: The adorable ones rejoice with delight, milking the streams of Ṛta that yield sweetly; come hither today, O ye of one accord, to the greatest of your great riches, to where ye stand.

sanskrit: evā no agne vikṣv ā daśasya tvayā vayaṁ sahasāvann āskrāḥ | rāyā yujā sadhamādo ariṣṭā yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Thus, O Agni, honour us among the peoples; with thee, O mighty one, we are unharmed; allied with riches, rejoicing together, unscathed — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: dadhikrāṁ vaḥ prathamam aśvinoṣasam agniṁ samiddham bhagam ūtaye huve | indraṁ viṣṇum pūṣaṇam brahmaṇas patim ādityān dyāvāpṛthivī apaḥ svaḥ ||
english: For your aid I invoke first Dadhikrāvan, the Aśvins, Uṣas, Agni well-kindled, and Bhaga; Indra, Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sunlight.

sanskrit: dadhikrām u namasā bodhayanta udīrāṇā yajñam upaprayantaḥ | iḷāṁ devīm barhiṣi sādayanto 'śvinā viprā suhavā huvema ||
english: Rousing Dadhikrāvan with homage, raising their voices as they advance upon the sacrifice, seating the divine Iḷā upon the sacred grass — O inspired poets, we invoke the well-invoked Aśvins.

sanskrit: dadhikrāvāṇam bubudhāno agnim upa bruva uṣasaṁ sūryaṁ gām | bradhnam mam̐ścator varuṇasya babhruṁ te viśvāsmad duritā yāvayantu ||
english: Being awake I address Dadhikrāvan, Agni, Uṣas, Sūrya, and the Dawn-cow; the vast yellow one, the tawny steer of the two heavens and of Varuṇa — may they drive all evil far from us.

sanskrit: dadhikrāvā prathamo vājy arvāgre rathānām bhavati prajānan | saṁvidāna uṣasā sūryeṇādityebhir vasubhir aṅgirobhiḥ ||
english: Dadhikrāvan the prize-winner comes first to the fore of the chariots, knowing the way; in accord with Uṣas, with Sūrya, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases.

sanskrit: ā no dadhikrāḥ pathyām anaktv ṛtasya panthām anvetavā u | śṛṇotu no daivyaṁ śardho agniḥ śṛṇvantu viśve mahiṣā amūrāḥ ||
english: May Dadhikrāvan anoint our path for us, that we may follow the path of Ṛta; may Agni, the divine host, hear us; may all the wise and mighty ones hear.

sanskrit: ā devo yātu savitā suratno 'ntarikṣaprā vahāmāno aśvaiḥ ||haste dadhāno naryā purūṇi niveśayañ ca prasuvañ ca bhūma ||
english: Let the god Savitṛ come hither, rich in true gifts, filling the midair, borne by his horses; holding in his hand many heroic gifts, both bringing to rest and urging on all beings.

sanskrit: ud asya bāhū śithirā bṛhantā hiraṇyayā divo antām̐ anaṣṭām | nūnaṁ so asya mahimā paniṣṭa sūraś cid asmā anu dād apasyām ||
english: His two broad, outstretched, golden arms, unfailing, reach to the ends of heaven; truly his greatness is to be praised — even the Sun has followed his course of activity.

sanskrit: sa ghā no devaḥ savitā sahāvā sāviṣad vasupatis vasūni | viśrayamāṇo amatiṁ urūcīm martabhojanaṁ adha rāsate naḥ ||
english: May that god Savitṛ, mighty of impulsion, the lord of riches, bestow riches upon us; spreading abroad the vast abundance, he then grants us the food allotted to mortals.

sanskrit: imā giraḥ savitāraṁ sujihvam pūrṇagabhastim īḻate supāṇim | citraṁ vayo bṛhad asme dadhātu yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: These hymns praise Savitṛ of fair tongue, full-handed, beautiful-palmed; may he bestow bright, ample sustenance upon us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ kṣipreṣave devāya svadhāvne | aṣāḻhāya sahamānāya vedhase tigmāyudhāya bharatā śṛṇotu naḥ ||
english: These songs for Rudra of the firm bow, the swift-arrowed god, self-nourishing, unconquered, all-enduring, wise, sharp-weaponed — sing them; let him hear us.

sanskrit: sa hi kṣayeṇa kṣamyasya janmanaḥ sāmrājyena divyasya cetati | avann avantīr upa no duraś carānamīvo rudra jāsu no bhava ||
english: For with sovereign rule over earthly creatures, and with lordship over the divine, he governs; be thou, O Rudra, free from anger, our protector at our doors, come to our aid — be gracious to our offspring.

sanskrit: yā te didyud avasṛṣṭā divas pari kṣmayā carati pari sā vṛṇaktu naḥ | sahasraṁ te svapivāta bheṣajā mā nas tokeṣu tanayeṣu rīriṣaḥ ||
english: Thy lightning-bolt that has been shot and ranges abroad over the earth — may it pass us by; O thou of good sleep, thy thousand remedies exist — injure us not in our children and our offspring.

sanskrit: mā no vadhī rudra mā parā dā mā te bhūma prasitau hīḻitasya | ā no bhaja barhiṣi jīvaśaṁse yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Strike us not, O Rudra, nor abandon us; let us not be caught in the snare of thee when wrathful; grant us a share at the sacred grass, in our hymn of life — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: āpo yaṁ vaḥ prathamaṁ devayanta indrapānam ūrmim akṛṇvateḻaḥ | taṁ vo vayaṁ śucim aripram adya ghṛtapruṣam madhumantaṁ vanema ||
english: O Waters, the wave which the god-loving Iḷā first fashioned for Indra's drinking — that pure, stainless, ghee-sprinkling, honey-sweet wave of yours we now claim.

sanskrit: tam ūrmim āpo madhhumattamaṁ vo 'pāṁ napād avatv āśuhemā | yasmin indro vasubhir mādayāte tam aśyāma devayanto vo adya ||
english: May Apāṁ Napāt, swift in impulse, protect that sweetest wave of yours, O Waters — the wave in which Indra rejoices with the Vasus; may we who love the gods attain that wave of yours today.

sanskrit: śatapavitrāḥ svadhayā madantīr devīr devānām api yanti pāthaḥ | tā indrasya na minanti vratāni sindhubhyo havyaṁ ghṛtavaj juhota ||
english: The divine Waters, purified by a hundred streams, rejoicing with their own power, reach the realm of the gods; they do not transgress Indra's ordinances — offer the oblation, rich in ghee, to the rivers.

sanskrit: yāḥ sūryo raśmibhir ātatāna yābhya indro aradat gātum ūrmim | te sindhavo varivo dhātanā no yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Those which the Sun has spread with his rays, those for whom Indra carved a path, a wave — O rivers, grant us wide space — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: ṛbhukṣaṇo vājā mādayadhvam asme naro maghavānaḥ sutasya | ā vo 'rvācaḥ kratavo na yātāṁ vibhvo rathaṁ naryaṁ vartayantu ||
english: O Ṛbhukṣan, O Vājas, rejoice in us — you heroes, generous ones, in the pressed Soma; may your resolves come hither toward us; may the Vibhvans turn the heroic chariot.

sanskrit: ṛbhur ṛbhubhir abhi vaḥ syāma vibhvo vibhubhiḥ śavasā śavāṁsi | vājo asmām̐ avatu vājasātāv indreṇa yujā taruṣema vṛtram ||
english: May we, through the Ṛbhus, be Ṛbhu-like for you; through the Vibhvans may we prevail with great strength; may Vāja protect us in the winning of prizes — yoked with Indra, may we overcome the foe.

sanskrit: te cid dhi pūrvīr abhi santi śāsā viśvām̐ arya uparatāti vanvan | indro vibhvāṁ ṛbhukṣā vājo aryaḥ śatror mithātyā kṛṇavan vi nṛmṇam ||
english: For even they have many commandments that prevail, winning over all foes and overcoming resistance; may Indra with Vibhvan, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and Ārya, through mutual combat, shatter the enemy's might.

sanskrit: nū devāso varivaḥ kartanā no bhūta no viśve 'vase sajoṣāḥ | sam asme iṣaṁ vasavo dadīran yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Now, O gods, make wide space for us; be all of one accord for our protection; may the Vasus bestow refreshment upon us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

sanskrit: samudrajyeṣṭhāḥ salilasya madhyāt punānā yanty aniviśamānāḥ | indro yā vajrī vṛṣabho rarāda tā āpo devīr iha mām avantu ||
english: Flowing from the midst of the flood, purifying themselves, led by the ocean, never resting — those divine Waters that Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, has cleft open — may they protect me here.

sanskrit: yā āpo divyā uta vā sravanti khanitrimā uta vā yāḥ svayaṁjāḥ | samudrārthā yāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakās tā āpo devīr iha mām avantu ||
english: Those divine Waters that flow from heaven, or those that flow in channels dug by man, or those that spring up of themselves — pure, cleansing, making their way to the ocean — may those divine Waters protect me here.

sanskrit: yāsāṁ rājā varuṇo yāti madhye satyānṛte avāpaśyañ janānām | madhuscutaḥ śucayo yāḥ pāvakās tā āpo devīr iha mām avantu ||
english: Those in whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men — honey-dripping, pure, and cleansing — may those divine Waters protect me here.

sanskrit: yāsu rājā varuṇo yāsu somo viśve devā yāsūrjam madanti | vaiśvānaro yāsv agniḥ praviṣṭas tā āpo devīr iha mām avantu ||
english: Those in which King Varuṇa dwells, in which Soma dwells, in which all the gods take delight in their vigour, into which Agni Vaiśvānara has entered — may those divine Waters protect me here.

sanskrit: ā mām mitrāvaruṇeha rakṣataṁ kulāyayad viśvayan mā na ā gan | ajakāvaṁ durdṛśīkaṁ tiro dadhe mā mām padyena rapasā vidat tsaruḥ ||
english: Protect me here, O Mitra and Varuṇa; let not the nesting, all-pervading one come upon me; I conceal the ill-formed, ugly thing — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.

sanskrit: yad vijāman paruṣi vandanam bhuvad aṣṭhīvantau pari kulphau ca dehat | agniṣ ṭac chocan apa bādhatām ito mā mām padyena rapasā vidat tsaruḥ ||
english: Whatever knotty obstruction may exist in the joints, whatever may cleave around the knees and ankles — let blazing Agni drive that away from here — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.

sanskrit: yac chalmalau bhavati yan nadīṣu yad oṣadhībhyaḥ pari jāyate viṣam | viśve devā nir itas tat suvantu mā mām padyena rapasā vidat tsaruḥ ||
english: Whatever poison exists in the silk-cotton tree, whatever is in the rivers, whatever venom arises from the plants — let all the gods press that out from here — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.

sanskrit: yāḥ pravato nivata udvata udanvatīr anudakāś ca yāḥ | tā asmabhyam payasā pinvamānāḥ śivā devīr aśipadā bhavantu sarvā nadyo aśimidā bhavantu ||
english: Those Waters that flow downward, those that flow upward, those that flow along ridges, those that are full of water and those that are dry — flowing with milk for our good, may they be auspicious and divinely benign, unhindering of foot; may all the rivers be ungrudging of food.
